transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-04
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Talia Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Neill (Kestra Platform), Dr. Asha Rao (Kestra GenAI), Miguel Santos (Kestra Security), Priya Kapoor (Kestra SRE)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hi everyone thanks for carving out the time, can I do a quick roll call?
[00:08] Liam O'Neill: Liam here, hi Maya
[00:10] Dr. Asha Rao: Asha on the call
[00:12] Miguel Santos: Miguel, security
[00:13] Priya Kapoor: Priya SRE
[00:15] Maya Chen: perfect, ravi and talia from our side too, we'll keep this to the POC scoping but happy to field security questions.
[00:22] Ravi Patel: quick agenda, cover connectivity options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region residency requirements, define success criteria (latency/cost/throughput), then benchmarks and timelines and owners.
[00:34] Dr. Asha Rao: great, the main driver for Kestra is that some of our data is treated like PHI under internal rules; we need guaranteed region locking — requests and any derived embeddings must not leave eu-west-1. is that doable?
[00:47] Ravi Patel: absolutely we support region pinning for Private deployments and can constrain Hosted routing to eu-west-1 for the POC. two options for networking: classic VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink. both can be configured to prevent internet egress, but differ in routing and operational ownership.
[01:02] Miguel Santos: quick clarify, by "prevent internet egress" you mean we won't have traffic routed to other regions or aws public endpoints? we also need to ensure logs and metrics don't contain raw prompt text in the telemetry.
[01:16] Talia Ortiz: yes, we can offer redaction options and store audit logs in customer-controlled S3 via KMS; we'll share the security deck.
[01:25] Maya Chen: can we go through tradeoffs quickly: vpc peering is straightforward but requires overlapping CIDR planning, PrivateLink gives you interface endpoints and is easier to lock down from a security group perspective. ravi?
[01:37] Ravi Patel: yep. in detail: VPC peering is L3 routing, good for high-throughput low-latency — less NAT overhead — but you need to manage route tables and ensure no overlapping IP ranges. PrivateLink gives you an ENI in your VPC; it's slightly higher Latency due to the NLB/ENI chain but provides armor against accidental routing to public subnets and is preferred by security teams for strict tenancy. For the POC we can run both in parallel if you want to compare actual latency.
[02:05] Priya Kapoor: we would like both run in parallel for benchmarking. we can stand up a small test VPC. what's realistic to expect for added latency for PrivateLink?
[02:16] Ravi Patel: ballpark 5-25ms additional p99 depending on region and path. for eu-west-1 we often see 8-12ms for 512-token calls in our internal tests when using interface endpoints. but your real world could differ, hence the benchmark.
[02:33] Liam O'Neill: important: our service mesh already does mutual TLS and we do strict ingress/egress proxies. how do we handle client auth and certs?
[02:43] Ravi Patel: we support mTLS for PrivateLink + client certs; alternatively you can use token-based auth over the PrivateLink path. for KMS, we support AWS KMS key wrapping for customer-managed keys — that's required for your compliance.
[02:57] Miguel Santos: about logs — will Redwood ever receive raw prompts? we need to be able to turn off any persistence of raw prompt text and only keep token-level metadata and hashes for auditing.
[03:10] Talia Ortiz: for Private deployments we can disable prompt persistence; for hosted we have retention controls and redaction. we'll include the specific config we used with other regulated customers.
[03:20] Dr. Asha Rao: success criteria: we want 99th percentile latency < 200ms for 512-token round trips at 50 rps sustained, error rate < 0.5% 5xxs, and no cross-region egress. cost is secondary but we'd like a working estimate. is that feasible?
[03:41] Ravi Patel: sounds measurable. note that 50 rps at 512 tokens is fairly heavy — batching will significantly affect cost/latency tradeoffs. two questions: is 50 rps steady or bursty? and what's your concurrency model?
[03:53] Liam O'Neill: a mix — baseline 10 rps with scheduled peaks to 50 rps over 30s windows. concurrency per client is low, but parallel callers across services will make total concurrency ~40.
[04:07] Ravi Patel: for POC benchmarking we'll model baseline 10 rps + 5x burst (to 50 rps) and run 10-minute sustained phases and short 30s bursts to simulate spikes. we'll collect p50/p95/p99 across batch sizes.
[04:19] Maya Chen: can you outline what we need from Kestra for sizing?
[04:23] Ravi Patel: please provide: token distribution (avg and 95th token lengths), expected request rate by hour, a representative prompt set (10-50 prompts), and any special function/tool calls. we'll provide a spreadsheet template.
[04:36] Liam O'Neill: we can export that by Monday; will include differences between dev and prod.
[04:41] Miguel Santos: network detail: we will not permit any outbound traffic from the VPC except to specific Redwood ENIs/cidrs. we also have DLP where any payload with certain regulators is blocked — will that affect the flow?
[04:54] Ravi Patel: you can whitelist ENIs; for DLP we recommend using an egress inspection step before calls or call the Redwood endpoint from an internal proxy that strips sensitive fields, we can help with example proxies.
[05:08] Dr. Asha Rao: regarding embeddings: we require that embeddings derived from our data remain in eu-west-1 and be stored in your private deployment attached to our cluster. can you guarantee no replication outside the pinned region?
[05:21] Talia Ortiz: yes for Private deployments we can guarantee region-local storage. for Hosted we can provide a dedicated eu-west-1 tenant and certify the data flow, but the contract must specify no cross-region backups.
[05:34] Maya Chen: note, POC is to validate connectivity and SLOs, not long-term storage; but we will show proof-of-concept for region lockdown and KMS integration.
[05:44] Ravi Patel: on benchmarks: suggested plan — 1) baseline single-threaded runs for latency profiles (no batching), 2) throughput runs with realistic batching configuration, 3) spike/run-to-failure tests to characterize graceful degradation. we'll measure tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and p99 latency.
[06:02] Liam O'Neill: can you share a sample benchmark sheet so we can fill in expected traffic?
[06:06] Ravi Patel: yes I'll share a sheet: https://redwood.test/benchmarks/kestra-poc.xlsx (placeholder) with tabs for token profile, rps scenarios, and raw logs.
[06:14] Priya Kapoor: timeline question — how long to stand up a private endpoint on our VPC for the POC?
[06:20] Maya Chen: typically we do a 5-7 business day setup for PrivateLink if CIDRs and IAM are ready; VPC peering is faster, 2-3 days, but depends on network approvals.
[06:31] Miguel Santos: our network approvals take 3 business days once we submit the ticket; so sequence wise we'll aim for a benchmark window in the week of 2025-06-16 if we get assets by 6/9.
[06:41] Ravi Patel: that aligns. we'll reserve a 2-hour window for an initial latency benchmark and a separate 4-hour throughput window.
[06:50] Dr. Asha Rao: do you have any concerns about tokenization differences across models affecting latency? we may evaluate two models for quality vs latency.
[06:59] Ravi Patel: yes tokenization affects token counts. we'll run identical prompt loads on both models and normalize by output tokens. also we'll capture model variant switching time as part of rollout testing.
[07:10] Liam O'Neill: about rollouts — we want canary routing between a quantized variant and a higher-accuracy float variant. how does Redwood handle automatic fallback if the canary hits errors?
[07:21] Talia Ortiz: Redwood has an automated fallback policy: if model A crosses an error threshold we can route traffic to model B automatically. that's configurable per route. we'll propose a canary configuration for the POC.
[07:33] Miguel Santos: audit trails: we need per-request audit logs with request id, model version, routing decisions, and pointer to encrypted prompt hash. can those logs be shipped to our S3 with KMS?
[07:44] Ravi Patel: yes, audit logs can be exported to customer S3 with KMS; raw prompts can be suppressed and only a hash retained. we also support pushing logs to Splunk/Datadog — but for compliance S3 + KMS is preferred.
[07:55] Priya Kapoor: small practical: our infra team uses Terraform. do you provide modules or examples for PrivateLink and peering setup?
[08:02] Maya Chen: yes we have sample Terraform modules and architecture diagrams; we'll add a Kestra-specific snippet to avoid IP overlap.
[08:10] Dr. Asha Rao: okay question on egress: if an internal microservice calls Redwood and our proxy strips PHI fields, is that considered safe or do you still need to see raw text to serve model?
[08:22] Ravi Patel: models need the prompt at inference time; if proxy strips PHI at field level and replaces with placeholders we can still work. you'll want to check for functional degradation. for the POC we can help run a test set with redacted fields to measure quality impact.
[08:37] Liam O'Neill: who does the KMS key rotation?
[08:40] Talia Ortiz: customer manages the CMK in AWS KMS; Redwood supports key ARN referencing and will re-wrap with customer CMK. rotation is customer-driven and supported.
[08:50] Miguel Santos: any issues with FIPS endpoints?
[08:52] Ravi Patel: we can route through FIPS endpoints for transport but the underlying runtime must be validated — we'll include FIPS compliance notes in the security deck.
[08:59] Maya Chen: quick pivot to success criteria: let's write a crisp POC success checklist: 1) connectivity established (PrivateLink or peering) with no internet egress 2) p99 latency <200ms for 512-token at target load 3) KMS integration validated 4) audit logs to S3 with prompt redaction 5) automated fallback works under induced failures. anyone add?
[09:21] Dr. Asha Rao: add embedding residency verification — show data stored and not replicated out of eu-west-1.
[09:27] Liam O'Neill: add cost estimate within 20% for projected monthly 100k requests.
[09:32] Maya Chen: good. we'll put those into the POC success doc.
[09:35] Ravi Patel: timeline recap: Redwood shares checklist and benchmark plan by 6/6, Kestra shares token distribution and CIDR info by 6/9, network approvals and Terraform snippets by 6/12, provisional benchmark windows week of 6/16.
[09:50] Miguel Santos: small security caveat: if DLP blocks certain patterns we need to know false positives could impact availability. can you simulate DLP rejection patterns during benchmarks?
[10:01] Ravi Patel: yes we can inject payloads representative of blocked patterns to validate fallback and QA.
[10:09] Priya Kapoor: testing environment — can we do a non-prod cluster in eu-west-1 that mirrors prod config for the POC?
[10:16] Talia Ortiz: yes, we'll provision a POC namespace with similar model versions and a scaled-down cluster.
[10:21] Dr. Asha Rao: on measurement—please confirm what metrics you'll provide back.
[10:26] Ravi Patel: we'll provide p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/sec, batching statistics, error rates, routing decisions, and cost estimate per 1k tokens. all in the benchmark sheet plus raw logs for a week.
[10:40] Liam O'Neill: what about termination of data after POC? we want a documented process for wiping embedded vectors and logs.
[10:47] Talia Ortiz: we have a documented data disposal procedure: we can securely delete keys and request we perform a crypto-shred of stored objects. we'll share the SOP.
[10:55] Maya Chen: anything else on networking specifics?
[10:58] Miguel Santos: one ask: we need explicit CIDR ranges for the ENIs you'll place in our VPC so our firewall team can pre-approve.
[11:05] Ravi Patel: we'll provide those ranges and a Terraform snippet for PrivateLink that binds the endpoint service and shows SG rules.
[11:12] Dr. Asha Rao: can Redwood support canaries by percentage routing so we can route 5% to float model and 95% to quantized?
[11:20] Talia Ortiz: yes, that's standard. we'll show a rollout policy in the console and how metrics will drive rollback.
[11:27] Maya Chen: final logistics: I'll send an email with the checklist, the benchmark plan and links to Terraform examples. Can we tentatively book the 6/16 benchmark slot?
[11:36] Liam O'Neill: tentatively yes pending approvals and the sheet.
[11:39] Miguel Santos: once we get the CIDRs we'll open the NetOps ticket.
[11:43] Maya Chen: perfect. quick recap of owners and due dates — I'll capture as action items. thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
